biased_opinion.summary: Red Granite Grinder runs October 10, 2026 from Athens, Wisconsin with 20-, 50-, 100-, and 150-mile races. The Bedrock Bruiser starts at 7:00 AM and turns a remote Central Wisconsin gravel day into an ultra-distance pacing, fueling, repair, and weather problem. The organizer has not yet published the current route files or climbing total.
strengths: Red granite roads through dairy country
weaknesses: Current route files and climbing are not published

biased_opinion.bottom_line: The Bedrock Bruiser is one of the cheaper ways to buy a genuine 150-mile race problem. Come for the red granite and hardwood color; prepare for remote-road self-sufficiency and let the final organizer route—not an old edition—set gearing and tire details.

logistics.lodging_note: Athens small town—limited lodging. Book early.
logistics.parking: Confirm the final parking and transfer plan; the published start is 221 Caroline Street and the finish is Miltrim Farms
logistics.travel_summary: Athens is a small Central Wisconsin town. Book lodging or the organizer's Miltrim Farms camping early and verify how you will move between the downtown start and farm finish.
logistics.food_options: The finish joins the Miltrim Farms Fall Festival with food trucks; on-course aid details remain pending
logistics.camping: Miltrim Farms offers no-hookup weekend camping for $55 with portable toilets

course_description.character: Four distances leave downtown Athens and finish at Miltrim Farms. The 150-mile Bedrock Bruiser is the flagship: a full day on remote red granite and rural Wisconsin roads, with the final route and climbing still pending.

suffering_zones.name: Bedrock Bruiser: 150 Miles
suffering_zones.description: The organizer calls the 150-mile race a full-day battle on remote roads where fatigue, pacing, and nutrition matter.
suffering_zones.survival_strategy: Start below the pace the fresh legs invite, fuel from the first hour, and carry a repair and lighting system appropriate for the final rider instructions.

suffering_zones.name: Red Granite Backroads
suffering_zones.description: The organizer describes red granite gravel through dairy farms, rivers, creeks, and hardwood canopies; exact surface percentages are not yet published.
suffering_zones.survival_strategy: Use the final route to set tires, pressure, gearing, and resupply. Do not carry old-course assumptions into race week.

suffering_zones.name: October Exposure
suffering_zones.description: A long October day can begin cold and move through sun, wind, or rain before the farm finish.
suffering_zones.survival_strategy: Use the final forecast to prove layers, gloves, visibility, and waterproof storage without overpacking.

course_description.signature_challenge: Keeping food, fluid, pace, equipment, and attention intact across 150 October miles before the Miltrim Farms finish.

history.origin_story: IRONBULL developed Red Granite Grinder as a Central Wisconsin gravel event and moved the race to Athens before the current edition.
history.reputation: A regional Wisconsin fall race known for its 150-mile option, accessible shorter distances, and community finish.

marketplace_variables.race_hook: A 150-mile Wisconsin gravel day from downtown Athens to Miltrim Farms.
marketplace_variables.race_hook_detail: Remote red granite roads make pacing, fueling, repair capacity, and October layers part of the race.

logistics.explanation: The organizer publishes exact starts for all four distances, a downtown Athens start, a Miltrim Farms finish, active registration, and weekend camping. Parking, packet pickup, aid, cutoff, and transfer details remain pending, so logistics are promising rather than complete.

length.explanation: The official 150-mile Bedrock Bruiser earns the maximum length score on distance alone. The same event also offers 100, 50, and 20 miles, but the flagship plan targets the full-day ultra-distance race.

technicality.explanation: The current organizer page promises red granite gravel and rural backroads but does not publish technical sectors or a final route. A 2/5 holds the race in nontechnical-to-moderate territory until current route files justify more.

elevation.explanation: The organizer does not publish a current climbing total or profile. The conservative 1/5 is retained provisionally and must be revisited when the final 2026 route appears; no old-edition elevation number is carried forward.

climate.explanation: An October 10 start in Central Wisconsin can span a cold morning, sun, wind, or rain across the full-day 150-mile window. The exposure is meaningful but not an extreme-climate event, so it remains 3/5.

altitude.explanation: Athens, Wisconsin presents no material altitude-acclimatization demand. The race-day problems are duration, surface, weather, fueling, and self-sufficiency.

adventure.explanation: The organizer frames the course around remote rural roads, dairy farms, rivers, creeks, and hardwood canopies. That is a real regional adventure, though current route details are not specific enough to support a higher score.

prestige.explanation: Red Granite Grinder has an established regional identity and the organizer cites outside recognition among Wisconsin cycling events, but it does not carry national championship or destination-race prestige.

race_quality.explanation: Four distances, distinct starts, active registration, a named flagship, and a festival finish show a real operation. Missing current route, aid, cutoff, parking, and packet details keep race quality at 3/5 until the rider packet lands.

experience.explanation: A downtown start, red granite farm roads, hardwood color, river corridors, and a fall-festival finish create a coherent Wisconsin experience. It is distinctive regionally without relying on unconfirmed course spectacles.

community.explanation: The race finishes inside the Miltrim Farms Fall Festival with food trucks and family activities, offers free kids registration, and sells simple weekend camping at the venue. The community is part of the event design, not an afterthought.

field_depth.explanation: Registration includes age/division, bike-category, and gender fields, but the organizer has not published a 2026 field list or elite roster. A middle regional-field score is the honest ceiling.

value.explanation: $75 before processing fees for the 150-mile race, $55 for 100 or 50 miles, $25 for 20 miles, and a free kids ride are unusually strong current values for a supported event day and festival finish.

expenses.explanation: $55 no-hookup weekend camping at the finish controls lodging cost, while Athens remains a driving destination with limited rooms. The separate start and finish may add transport friction but not destination-event pricing.

final_verdict.one_liner: A genuine 150-mile Wisconsin gravel problem at a regional-race price, ending inside a farm festival.
final_verdict.should_you_race: Race it if a long red-granite day, affordable entry, and community finish matter more than national prestige. Use the 100-, 50-, or 20-mile race if the 150-mile self-sufficiency problem is not the day you want.
final_verdict.alternatives: UNBOUND 200 for national field depth, Gravel Worlds for a bigger Midwest destination event, or Barry-Roubaix for a shorter and denser race experience.
